historical_cultural_context.text: Mount Rushmore National Memorial, near Keystone in South Dakota's Black Hills, was carved into granite between 1927 and 1941 under sculptor Gutzon Borglum. His son Lincoln Borglum finished the work after Borglum died in March 1941, and funding limits ended the carving. The sculpture depicts four U.S. presidents, Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt and Lincoln, to symbolise the nation's first 150 years. The mountain was known to the Lakota as Six Grandfathers, and the site is on land sacred to them, so the monument remains controversial.

historical_cultural_context.text: Big Ben is the nickname of the Great Bell, and by extension the clock tower at the north end of the Palace of Westminster. The tower was named the Clock Tower until 2012, when it was renamed Elizabeth Tower for Elizabeth II's Diamond Jubilee. It was built as part of Charles Barry's design for the new Palace of Westminster, after the old palace was largely destroyed by fire on 16 October 1834. Barry turned to Augustus Pugin for the tower's design. Construction began in 1843 and the tower was completed in 1859. It stands about 96 m tall. The palace is regarded as a major monument of neo-Gothic architecture.

historical_cultural_context.text: The Hawa Mahal, or Palace of Winds, was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh of Jaipur, grandson of the city's founder Jai Singh II. It was designed by Lal Chand Ustad. The red and pink sandstone facade has 953 jharokhas arranged like a honeycomb. They let royal women watch street life without being seen (purdah) and also ventilate the building. It is described as an extension of the City Palace leading to the zenana. Its style blends Rajput and Mughal influences. Sources say it was inspired by the Khetri Mahal and is shaped like the crown of Lord Krishna.

historical_cultural_context.text: Ahu Tongariki is the largest ahu on Rapa Nui. Its moai were toppled during the island's civil wars, and a 1960 tsunami from the Chilean earthquake swept the statues and topknots inland. It was substantially restored in the 1990s by a University of Chile team led by Claudio Cristino and Patricia Vargas Casanova, with Japanese funding and a crane donated by Tadano. It now has 15 moai, one of which weighs about 86 tonnes. Tongariki was the main centre of the Hotu-iti clan. Only one of its statues wears a red scoria pukao, and the others' topknots lie scattered nearby. Pukao are generally interpreted as representing a chieftain's topknot, carved from red scoria quarried at Puna Pau.

img8.jpg.reasoning_evidence: The moai style and the ahu masonry point to Rapa Nui. Searches confirmed that Ahu Tongariki has a long row of 15 restored moai and that only one wears a red pukao, second from the right in front view. That matches the topknotted figure being second from the end of the row in this angled view. The observation record's mention of a grassy, treeless setting is also consistent with the sources. The view shows only eight statues, so the full row is not confirmed. The identification therefore rests on the site-level uniqueness of the single-topknot arrangement, which is strong but not absolute. The mounds in the foreground were not verified against any source.

historical_cultural_context.text: Harmandir Sahib is the holiest gurdwara of Sikhism. Sources describe the sarovar being excavated from about 1570 and the temple being built under Guru Arjan, completed around 1601–1604, when the Adi Granth was installed. The architecture blends Hindu (Rajput) and Indo-Islamic (Mughal) styles. The lower level is marble and the upper level is gold-leafed copper, topped by an inverted-lotus dome. It has four doors, symbolising openness to all. Sources vary on some details, such as the quantity of gold and exact dates.

historical_cultural_context.text: The Scott Monument is a Victorian Gothic monument to Sir Walter Scott in Princes Street Gardens. Construction began in 1840 and the monument was inaugurated in 1846. Kemp drowned in the Union Canal in 1844, before completion. John Steell's Carrara marble statue of Scott with his dog Maida sits beneath the spire. The monument is decorated with statues of Scott's characters and has a 287-step spiral stair to viewing galleries. The stone was reportedly expected to blacken, which suited the Gothic look.

historical_cultural_context.text: Fushimi Inari Taisha in southern Kyoto is the head shrine of the Inari deity, the Shinto god of rice. It is famous for its thousands of vermilion torii.
